 BananaBro & Boat Noodle Founder Tony Lim Dies
 He founded Boat Noodle in 2014 and BananaBro in 2018.

 The founder of BananaBro and Boat Noodle, Tony Lim, has died
 Both F&B brands shared condolence posts on social media today, 2 November, mourning Lim's passing and honouring his contributions to building the businesses and caring for his employees.
"It is with heavy hearts that we announce the passing of our beloved founder, Tony Lim.
"Tony had a vision — to bring Malaysia's banana leaf culture to the world. With his passion, generosity, and unwavering belief in that dream, he brought BananaBro to life.
"Tony gave more than just his vision. He gave his heart to the people and the journey he believed in.
"Though he is no longer with us, his dream lives on in every banana leaf we serve and every life he has touched.
"Thank you, Tony. Your passion inspired us, your generosity touched us, and your legacy will live on," read BananaBro's Instagram post .
 View this post on Instagram 
 A post shared by BananaBro (@bananabromy) 
 Meanwhile, Art of Speed (AOS) Malaysia, an automobile and art event organiser, also paid tribute to Lim in a Facebook post
 "The AOS family is deeply saddened by the passing of Tony Lim.
"Thank you for being part of Art of Speed Malaysia and for the memories shared with the community. You will be dearly missed.
"Our heartfelt condolences to his family and loved ones. Rest in peace, Tony," read the post published yesterday, 1 November.
 Lim was a F&B entrepreneur who started out in his family's trucking business in 2005
 According to Prestige Online , Lim's family business, E.H. Utara Holdings, boasts regional presence with offices in Malaysia, Thailand, Singapore, Cambodia, and Laos.
The company offers a comprehensive logistics solutions, including in-land and cross-border transportation, warehousing, and distribution.
According to his LinkedIn profile, Lim joined E.H. Utara Holdings in 2005 and served as its chief executive director.
He went on to found Boat Noodle in 2014 and BananaBro in 2018.
